sections.title: Molecular profile of cervical adenocarcinoma
sections.intro: Cervical ADC is **two diseases** (IECC / WHO 2020): HPV-associated (usual-type 73%, mucinous 9%) and HPV-independent (gastric-type 10%, clear cell 3%, mesonephric rare) [6]. **NHPVA changes management**: older, higher-stage, worse survival (gastric-type 5-yr DSS 42% vs 91%) [7–10]; clear cell behaves like gastric-type [11]. A p16−/HPV− tumour in an older woman is gastric-type until proved otherwise [9,10,20]; IHC panel: Distinguish endocervical adenocarcinoma from endometrioid in immuohistochemical markers.

cells: HPVA usual-type **73%**; HPVA mucinous 9%; **gastric-type 10%**; clear cell 3%; adenocarcinoma NOS 2%; endometrioid 3 cases, all NHPVA. p16 block-positive 90% and HPV RNA ISH-positive 95% of usual-type vs 37% and 3% of NHPVA; NHPVA older and larger (P < 0.001) [6]. Toronto series (n = 87): HPVA 82% (usual 72%, mucinous NOS 14%, ISMC 11%), NHPVA 18% (gastric 12/16 = 71%, clear cell and mesonephric 2 each = 12%); NHPVA carried more lymphovascular invasion, more advanced stage and more invasive pattern C (all P < 0.001) and worse disease-specific survival, and among HPVA subtypes **ISMC had the worst DFS and DSS** [8]

Alpha-7 (HPV18) clade is over-represented in adenocarcinoma relative to SCC; the TCGA adenocarcinoma-rich integrative cluster was separate from the keratin-low and keratin-high squamous clusters, and a small **endometrial-like, predominantly HPV-negative** cluster carried high KRAS, ARID1A and PTEN mutation frequencies [13]. Across the 178-tumour core set 169 (95%) were HPV-positive: alpha-9 types 120 (67%, of which 103 HPV16), **alpha-7 types 45 (25%, of which 27 HPV18)**, HPV-negative 9 (5%); **A7 types were enriched in the keratin-low and adenocarcinoma clusters (P = 5 × 10⁻⁴)** and non-European HPV16 variants were associated with adenocarcinoma (OR 5.3, P = 3 × 10⁻³). Per-histology genotype counts appear only in Supplementary Table 3 [13]

Adenocarcinoma (n = 24, exome): ELF3 13%, CBFB 8%; fewer APOBEC-type Tp*C substitutions than SCC [14]. Oncomap (80 tumours; whole-series PIK3CA 31.3%, KRAS 8.8%, EGFR 3.8%): PIK3CA 25% in adenocarcinoma vs 37.5% in SCC (P = .33); **KRAS 17.5% vs 0%** (P = .01); EGFR 0% vs 7.5%; PIK3CA mutation associated with shorter survival (HR 9.1, 2.8–29.5) [15]. Gastric-type (n = 182, 2014–2025): **TP53 mutation, PTEN deletion and STK11 mutation** the most prevalent alterations, with marked genetic heterogeneity but a **low level of genomic instability**; 64% stage IIB–IV at diagnosis, 5-yr survival 41% (IIB–IV) vs 85% (I–IIA), P < 0.05; LVSI 49.6%, nodal metastasis 42.0%, ovarian metastasis 29.3%; overall 5-yr survival 57% and recurrence 23% [109]

**Usual-type adenocarcinoma 60% (35/58)** vs SCC 91% (397/437) in 647 profiled cervical carcinomas [16]; at a **≥5% tumour-cell cutoff, 83 of 154 SCC (54%) vs 7 of 49 adenocarcinomas (14%)** were PD-L1-positive (P < 0.001), and PD-L1-positive tumour-associated macrophages were present in 53% vs 12% (P < 0.001), and PD-L1-positive macrophages predicted worse DSS in adenocarcinoma (P = 0.014) [17]. **HPV-independent adenocarcinoma: CPS ≥1 in 14/44 (31.8%)**, TPS ≥1% in 12/44 (27.3%); positivity by either score tracked a high tumour-infiltrating-lymphocyte percentage (P < 0.001 for both) and **predicted worse survival**; MMR intact in 42/44 [18]. Trial screening: KEYNOTE-826 CPS ≥1 548/617 all histologies [1]; KEYNOTE-158 had 5 adenocarcinomas and 1 adenosquamous, all PD-L1-positive, responses not reported by histology [21]

Meta-analysis of ASCO/CAP-compliant studies (all cervical histologies): overexpression **5.7%** (1.5–11.7%), amplification 1.2% (0.0–5.8%); histology was not a significant moderator [19]. Gastric-type (13 cases found among 322 consecutive cervical cancers, Kyoto 2010–2016): **HER2 IHC equivocal in 6 and amplified in 1**; MUC6 positive in 13/13 and HIK1083 in 8/13; watery discharge, lower abdominal pain, CA19-9 elevation and nodal metastasis were all more frequent than in other histologies (P = 0.023, 0.040, 0.035, 0.027) [20]. Histology was not a significant moderator in the meta-analysis, so no adenocarcinoma-specific rate is derivable from it

Radical hysterectomy with BSO, stage IB–IIB (n = 3471): **adenocarcinoma 5.31% vs SCC 0.79%**; by stage IB 3.72%, IIA 5.26%, IIB 9.85% in adenocarcinoma vs 0.22%, 0.75%, 2.17% in SCC; 52 of 3471 overall (1.50%), and ovarian metastasis correlated with neither nodal involvement nor parametrial invasion, with a poor outcome regardless of stage or histology [22]. Gastric-type series (n = 182): ovarian metastasis **29.3%**, an independent marker of worse PFS and OS even in stage I–II [109]. Meta-analysis in early adenocarcinoma: ovarian metastasis 0% IA, 2.8% IB, 3.4% IIA, 11.8% IIB; preservation did not change OS (OR 1.00, 0.64–1.56) or PFS [23]; risk factors stage IIB (OR 4.64), deep stromal invasion (OR 10.63), nodal metastasis (OR 8.54), corpus invasion (OR 7.39), parametrial invasion (OR 9.72, 4.67–20.22), plus stage IIB vs I–IIA (OR 4.64, 2.11–10.23), deep stromal invasion (OR 10.63, 3.12–36.02), nodal metastasis (OR 8.54, 4.15–17.57) and corpus uteri invasion (OR 7.39, 3.69–14.78) [24]
Membrane expression ≥1% in 93.3% of 404 assessed in innovaTV 301, all histologies; not an eligibility criterion [2]
HPV-independent adenocarcinoma: MSH2/MSH6 loss in 2/44, the other 42 MMR-intact [18]; usual-type frequency ⬜. TCGA hypermutation not reported by histology [13]

notes.title: Testing
notes.md:
- IECC type, p16 and HPV on every ADC: NHPVA removes fertility-sparing surgery and ovarian preservation [25] and predicts chemoresistance [101].
- PD-L1 CPS before first-line recurrent therapy: CPS <1 is expected in ADC [16,18].
- HER2 IHC at recurrence if T-DXd is considered [86]. Ovarian metastasis 5–7× SCC; preserve only in low-risk HPVA [22–25].

sections.title: 1. Adjuvant therapy after radical hysterectomy (FIGO 2009 IA2–IIA)
sections.intro: Split by pathological risk: **1A intermediate** (node-negative; ADC histology is not a GOG-92/263 criterion [28]) and **1B high** (nodes, margins or parametrium). Retrospective ADC series follow in italics.

cols.regimen: Pelvic RT (46 Gy/23 fx to 50.4 Gy/28 fx) vs no further treatment
cols.pop: Stage IB, node-negative, ≥2 of: >1/3 stromal invasion, capillary lymphatic space involvement, clinical tumour diameter ≥4 cm
cols.hist: **ADC subgroup reported**: adeno/adenosquamous 59 (34 RT, 25 observation). Recurrence **8.8% (3/34) vs 44.0% (11/25)**; RT-by-histology interaction HR **0.23 (90% CI 0.07–0.74)**, P = 0.019 — the RT benefit was concentrated in non-squamous tumours. By pure histology: adenocarcinoma **0/16 recurred with RT vs 4/11 (36.4%) with observation**, adenosquamous 3/18 (16.7%) vs 7/14 (50.0%), squamous 21/103 (20.4%) vs 32/115 (27.8%) [27]
cols.hr: All patients: recurrence 0.54 (90% CI 0.35–0.81), P = 0.007; progression or death 0.58 (90% CI 0.40–0.85); OS 0.70 (90% CI 0.45–1.05), P = 0.074, NS. Adeno-specific OS not reported — deaths (Table 5) are not tabulated by cell type
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 adverse events 6% vs 2.1%. Authors: "RT appears to be particularly beneficial for patients with adenocarcinoma or adenosquamous histologies" [27]. Subgroup of 59

cols.regimen: Pelvic RT (median 50.4 Gy; conformal or IMRT) + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×6 vs RT alone
cols.pop: Stage I–IIA (FIGO 2009), intermediate-risk combinations after radical hysterectomy and lymphadenectomy
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: adenocarcinoma 24 (15.2%) vs 32 (20.3%), adenosquamous 8 (5.1%) vs 15 (9.5%) in the RT vs CRT arms; histology subgroup not reported (subgroups were by RT modality)
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 adverse events 43% vs 15% (P < 0.01). Non-squamous imbalance (20.3% vs 34.8%) favoured the RT arm

cols.regimen: *Radical hysterectomy + pelvic LND → pelvic RT ≥45 Gy (median 50.4 Gy; brachytherapy 219/1323 = 16.6% at a median 24 Gy; concurrent chemotherapy 492 = 37.2%); no NACT*
cols.pop: *FIGO IB–IIA, intermediate and high risk mixed; 10 Korean centres, median follow-up 75.7 mo (2.2–257.9)*
cols.hist: ***ADC subgroup reported (prognostic, retrospective)***: *5-yr RFS **SCC 83.7%, adenocarcinoma 66.5%, adenosquamous 79.6%** (P < 0.0001); 5-yr LRRFS 94.0% / 79.1% / 91.3%; recurrence 15.3% / **33.0%** / 18.5%; adenocarcinoma the only histology independently significant for all three endpoints*
cols.os: *5-yr OS **75.8% vs 87.6%** (histology P = 0.0028 univariate); multivariable OS HR **1.729 (1.085–2.617)**, P = 0.0195*
cols.tox: *Adenosquamous tracked SCC, not adenocarcinoma. Multivariable LRRFS HR for adenocarcinoma 2.312 (1.293–4.135), P = 0.0047; adenosquamous not significant for RFS (1.421, 0.688–2.936)*

cols.regimen: *Radical hysterectomy ± adjuvant RT or CCRT (regimens not different between histologies)*
cols.pop: *FIGO IB–IIA, 1994–2007, single centre; median follow-up 49.6 mo*
cols.hist: ***ADC subgroup reported (prognostic)***: *recurrence **14.4% (20/139) vs 5.7% (36/636)**, P < 0.001; distant recurrence 45.0% (9/20) vs 22.2% (8/36) of recurrences (P = .076), lymphatic 25.0% vs 50.0% (P = .068); death **10.8% (15/139) vs 2.7% (17/636)**, P < 0.001; LVSI 38.1% vs 27.3%; pure adenocarcinoma an independent factor for DFS and OS*
cols.os: *Multivariable OS HR **15.27 (3.74–62.43)**, P < 0.001 (wide CI — 15 vs 17 deaths)*
cols.tox: *Adenocarcinoma patients younger (median 44 vs 49 yr, P = .001). Within adenocarcinoma, grade II/III vs I separated DFS and OS univariately (P = .004, P < 0.001) but not after adjustment (P = 0.109, P = 0.287)*

cols.regimen: *Initial radiotherapy ± adjuvant hysterectomy*
cols.hist: ***ADC subgroup reported (prognostic, pre-chemoradiation era)***: *5-yr survival **72% vs 81%** (P < 0.01); tumours ≥4 cm (n = 903) **59% vs 73%** (P < 0.01); distant metastasis **37% vs 21%** (P < 0.01), pelvic recurrence 13% vs 17% (P = 0.16). Adenocarcinomas were more often < 4 cm (53% vs 47%)*
cols.hr: *Multivariate: for tumours ≥4 cm, adenocarcinoma carried an estimated **risk of death 1.9× that of SCC** (P < 0.01). In that subgroup survival tracked tumour size (P < 0.01) and lymphangiogram findings (P < 0.01), not age (P = 0.58) or exophytic vs endocervical morphology (P = 0.33)*
cols.tox: *The deficit is distant, not pelvic. Adjuvant hysterectomy in 165 patients with ≥4 cm tumours gave only a non-significant trend — **78% with vs 71% without**, P = 0.09 — so it did not close the histology gap*

sections.title: 1B. High risk (node-positive, margin-positive or parametrial involvement)

cols.regimen: Pelvic RT 49.3 Gy/29 fx + cisplatin 70 mg/m² D1 + 5-FU 1000 mg/m²/day ×4 days, q3w ×4 (2 concurrent, 2 after RT) vs RT alone
cols.pop: Stage IA2, IB, IIA after radical hysterectomy with positive pelvic nodes, positive margins or parametrial involvement
cols.hist: **ADC subgroup reported (figure only)**: adenocarcinoma 18 (14%) + adenosquamous 12 (9%) in CT+RT vs 13 (11%) + 7 (6%) in RT alone. On RT alone, adeno/adenosquamous (n = 23 in Fig 3) had worse PFS than SCC; **with chemotherapy the difference disappeared** (Fig 4); treatment-by-cell-type interaction P = .12 (PFS), .19 (OS). No non-squamous HR is printed — Figs 3 and 4 are Kaplan–Meier curves only
cols.hr: Printed RT vs CT+RT: PFS 2.01 (P = .003), OS 1.96 (P = .007); CI not printed
cols.tox: Grade 4 toxicity 27 episodes in 21 CT+RT patients vs 4 on RT. "Adenocarcinomas and adenosquamous carcinomas had a poorer prognosis in patients with at least one other poor prognostic factor" [29]

cols.regimen: *Same trial, retrospective univariate analysis*
cols.pop: *As above*
cols.hist: ***Included, not broken out***: *benefit of chemotherapy "not strongly associated" with histological type*
cols.pfs: *5-yr survival RT vs RT+CT by tumour size: ≤2 cm 77% vs 82%; >2 cm 58% vs 77%*
cols.tox: *Hypothesis-generating*

cols.regimen: Sequential chemoradiation (cisplatin 60–75 mg/m² + paclitaxel 135–175 mg/m² q21d, 2 cycles before and 2 after RT) vs concurrent weekly cisplatin 30–40 mg/m² + RT vs RT alone (45–50 Gy)
cols.pop: FIGO IB–IIA after radical hysterectomy with adverse pathological factors (intermediate and high risk mixed); 8 Chinese hospitals
cols.hist: **ADC subgroup reported**: adeno/adenosquamous **140 of 1048 (13.4%)**, squamous 908. Recurrence vs RT alone — SCRT **HR 0.294 (0.119–0.724)**, CCRT **HR 0.360 (0.151–0.859)** (recurrence 9/41 [22.0%] and 8/46 [17.4%] vs 17/53 [32.1%]); squamous SCRT 0.547 (0.357–0.839), CCRT 0.931 (0.635–1.365). The sequential-chemoradiation benefit was at least as large in non-squamous tumours
cols.pfs: 3-yr DFS SCRT **90.0% vs RT 82.0%**; SCRT vs CCRT 90.0% vs 85.0%
cols.hr: DFS SCRT vs RT **0.52 (0.35–0.76)**; SCRT vs CCRT 0.65 (0.44–0.96); cancer death SCRT vs RT 0.58 (0.35–0.95)
cols.tox: Concurrent weekly cisplatin did not improve DFS or cancer death over RT alone

cols.regimen: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC5 → pelvic RT 50.4 Gy vs RT + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m²
cols.pop: Stage IB–IIB after surgery, high risk
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: adenocarcinoma **35 (26.5%)** in the sequential paclitaxel–carboplatin arm vs **23 (17.6%)** in the concurrent cisplatin arm (P = 0.213); squamous 93 (70.5%) vs 104 (79.4%); histology subgroup not reported
cols.tox: Early termination 12.9% vs 32.1% (P = 0.001); more grade 3–4 haematological toxicity with CCRT

cols.regimen: *No adjuvant vs RT vs CCRT vs chemotherapy after surgery (retrospective, risk-stratified; preplanned secondary analysis of a Japanese nationwide cohort)*
cols.pop: *Stage I–II gastric-type adenocarcinoma after surgery; JSGO low-risk 17, intermediate 37, high-risk 48; median follow-up 46.2 mo*
cols.hist: ***ADC-only (gastric-type only), retrospective***: *adjuvant given to 63 — RT 22 (20.6%), CCRT 11 (11.8%), chemotherapy 30 (29.4%, 25/30 taxane–platinum); recurrence in **41 of 102** (local 17, distant 17, both 7). Intermediate risk — too few events for a median; **high risk — RT was the better arm on both endpoints***
cols.pfs: *High risk, RT as control: CCRT HR **2.514 (0.873–7.237)**, P = 0.088; chemotherapy HR **2.057 (0.818–5.17)**, P = 0.125. Intermediate risk (no events): no-adjuvant 0.867 (0.079–9.564), CCRT 5.158 (0.321–82.817), chemotherapy 3.767 (0.451–31.454)*
cols.os: *High risk, RT as control: CCRT HR **1.277 (0.358–4.558)**, P = 0.706; chemotherapy HR **1.791 (0.661–4.852)**, P = 0.252. Intermediate risk: no-adjuvant 0.872, CCRT 3.962, chemotherapy 1.15, all non-significant*
cols.hr: *no toxicity comparison; the 27 evaluable chemotherapy patients completed a median 6 cycles without toxicity-related complications*
cols.tox: *"Chemotherapy strategies, including CCRT as postoperative adjuvant therapy, tend to have a poor prognosis" in gastric-type. Every HR is non-significant and 6 high-risk patients without adjuvant therapy were excluded, so this is a trend in 102 patients, not a comparative result. In usual-type adenocarcinoma from the same cohort adjuvant therapy made no difference*

cols.regimen: Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + cisplatin 50 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC6 q3w ×6 vs CCRT (50.4 Gy + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m²)
cols.pop: Stage IB–IIB after radical hysterectomy with pelvic nodal metastasis and/or parametrial invasion
cols.hist: **Included**: SCC, adenocarcinoma and adenosquamous eligible
cols.tox: Design paper only; no PubMed results publication found (2026-09-16)

notes.title: Reading Table 1
notes.md:
- Adjuvant RT benefit concentrates in ADC (GOG-92 interaction HR 0.23) [27]; the GOG-109 non-squamous deficit closed with chemo [29]. Small subgroups, no ADC OS HR.
- Intermediate risk: adding cisplatin is unanswered (GOG-263 negative, histology imbalance) [28].
- High risk: cisplatin/5-FU CRT has the OS benefit [29]; STARS sequential chemo helped ADC at least as much [31].
- Retrospective: ADC recurs more and distantly [35–37]; adenosquamous tracks SCC [35].
- Gastric-type: CCRT no better than RT [34]. Surgery-first rests on a 46-patient Landoni subgroup (NS) [38].
- Context: MIS radical hysterectomy worse DFS [40]; simple hysterectomy OK ≤2 cm low risk [39]; ESGO fertility-sparing only for HPVA [25].

sections.title: 2. Primary treatment of locally advanced disease (FIGO 2008/2009 IB2–IVA; FIGO 2018 IB3–IVA)
2A. Definitive chemoradiation: backbone, schedule, induction and adjuvant chemotherapy

cols.regimen: Induction weekly carboplatin AUC2 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² ×6 → CCRT vs CCRT alone (weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×5 + 45–50.4 Gy EBRT + brachytherapy, EQD2 78–86 Gy)
cols.pop: FIGO 2008 IB1 node-positive, IB2, IIA, IIB, IIIB, IVA (IIB 70%, IIIB 11%; nodes positive 43%)
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: randomisation stratified by squamous vs non-squamous; non-squamous **44 (18%) vs 45 (18%)** (89/500, 17.8%); neither the paper nor its figures print a histology subgroup HR
cols.tox: Grade ≥3 adverse events 59% vs 48%; median 7 days from induction to CCRT

cols.regimen: RT + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×6 vs RT + cisplatin 50 mg/m² D1, D29 + 5-FU 4 g/m² 96-h + hydroxyurea (CFH) vs RT + hydroxyurea 3 g/m² twice weekly
cols.pop: Stage IIB, III, IVA with surgically negative para-aortic nodes
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: adenocarcinoma 13 (7.4%) / 11 (6.4%) / 6 (3.4%), adenosquamous 5 (2.8%) / 8 (4.6%) / 5 (2.8%) in the cisplatin / CFH / hydroxyurea arms (non-squamous 48/526, 9.1%); pooled with GOG-85, 123, 165 and 191 in the Rose 2014 row below
cols.hr: vs hydroxyurea — cisplatin: PFS 0.57 (0.42–0.78), OS **0.61 (0.44–0.85)**; CFH: PFS 0.55 (0.40–0.75), OS 0.58 (0.41–0.81). Long-term progression/death relative risk 0.57 (0.43–0.75) and 0.51 (0.38–0.67)
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 leukopenia ~23% (cisplatin) vs ~46% (CFH). Established weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m²

cols.regimen: RT + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² (max 70 mg/wk) ×6 → extrafascial hysterectomy vs RT → hysterectomy
cols.pop: Bulky (≥4 cm) stage IB, radiographically node-negative
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: adenocarcinoma 14 (8%) vs 9 (5%), adenosquamous 10 (5%) vs 17 (9%) in the RT vs combined arms; at 101 months the follow-up report counts adeno/adenosquamous 24 (13%) vs 26 (14%) [45]; no histology subgroup analysis in either report
cols.pfs: Recurrence 21% vs 37%; 72-mo alive and disease-free 71% vs 60%
cols.hr: Progression 0.51 (0.34–0.75), death 0.54 (0.34–0.86) (relative risks, 1999); at 101 mo adjusted death HR **0.63 (0.43–0.91)**
cols.tox: Any grade 3–4 AE 35% vs 13%. Adjuvant hysterectomy since discontinued

cols.regimen: Weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² + gemcitabine 125 mg/m² ×6 with EBRT 50.4 Gy → brachytherapy → cisplatin 50 mg/m² D1 + gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² D1, 8 ×2 vs weekly cisplatin CCRT → brachytherapy
cols.pop: Stage IIB–IVA, KPS ≥70
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: adenocarcinoma **17 (6.6%) vs 15 (5.9%)** (32/515, 6.2%); adenosquamous was pooled with squamous in the printed table; histology subgroup not reported
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 toxicity 86.5% vs 46.3% (P < .001); two changes at once (gemcitabine concurrent + adjuvant)

cols.regimen: Pelvic RT 45 Gy + cisplatin 75 mg/m² + 5-FU 4 g/m² 96-h ×3 vs extended-field (pelvic + para-aortic) RT alone
cols.pop: Stage IIB–IVA, or IB–IIA with tumour ≥5 cm or positive pelvic nodes; para-aortic nodes negative
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 176 (90%) vs 174 (90%); adeno/adenosquamous **19 vs 19** in the 2004 update [48] (~10% per arm); no histology subgroup analysis in either report
cols.hr: DFS event relative risk 0.48 (0.35–0.66); OS HR not printed
cols.tox: Acute grade 3–4 44% in the chemotherapy arm; two variables changed at once

cols.regimen: RT + cisplatin + 5-FU infusion vs RT + oral hydroxyurea
cols.pop: Stage IIB–IVA, negative para-aortic nodes
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: squamous 156 (88.1%) vs 179 (93.7%), adenocarcinoma 8 (4.5%) vs 6 (3.1%), adenosquamous 13 (7.3%) vs 6 (3.1%) in the cisplatin–5-FU vs hydroxyurea arms (non-squamous 12% vs 6.2%); histology subgroup not reported
cols.tox: Severe or life-threatening leukopenia 4% vs 24%

cols.regimen: Weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×5 CCRT → carboplatin AUC5 + paclitaxel 155 mg/m² q21d ×4 vs CCRT alone
cols.pop: FIGO 2008 IB1 node-positive, IB2, II, IIIB, IVA
cols.hist: **ADC subgroup reported (post hoc)**: adenocarcinoma 79 (17%) vs 68 (15%), adenosquamous 19 (4%) vs 12 (3%) in CRT vs CRT+ACT. Adenocarcinoma (n = 147): OS **HR 0.87 (0.46–1.64)** vs squamous/adenosquamous 0.90 (0.68–1.20), **interaction P = 0.98**; PFS 0.90 (0.55–1.48) vs 0.86 (0.68–1.10), interaction P = 0.94. 5-yr OS in adenocarcinoma 72% vs 71%; 5-yr PFS 54% vs 53%
cols.tox: Grade 3–4 neutropenia 20% vs 8%; 22% never started adjuvant chemotherapy

cols.regimen: RT + cisplatin 75 mg/m² q3w ×3 vs RT + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×6
cols.pop: Stage IIB–IVA
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: SCC 137 (90.1%) weekly vs 114 (81.4%) triweekly; adenocarcinoma 12 (7.9%) vs 20 (14.3%), adenosquamous 1 (0.7%) vs 2 (1.4%) — non-squamous 9.9% vs 18.6%; no histology subgroup analysis
cols.tox: Fewer grade 3–4 haematological toxicities with triweekly (P < 0.001); non-squamous imbalance against the triweekly arm

cols.regimen: RT + cisplatin 75 mg/m² q3w ×3 vs RT + weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² ×6
cols.pop: Stage IIB–IVA
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: the paper prints no histology distribution
cols.tox: Not confirmed by TACO [51]

cols.regimen: CCRT (cisplatin 40 mg/m² weekly × 5 with 42–48 Gy to point A) **+ one neoadjuvant cycle paclitaxel 135 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² before RT and two consolidation cycles after RT (q3w)** vs CCRT alone
cols.pop: Clinical FIGO IIB–IVA **cervical adenocarcinoma** (adenosquamous 10), 1998–2007; median follow-up 60 mo
cols.hist: **ADC-only trial** (the only randomised adenocarcinoma-only trial retrieved)
cols.pfs: Recurrence **126 (28.6%) with added chemotherapy vs 214**; PFS curves P = .004 (log-rank). Distant failure 63 vs 104 and central recurrence 63 vs 110 (both P < .005); pelvic failure 62 vs 100

Two inconsistencies as printed: the control-arm percentages do not match their own counts (226/440 given as 60.4%, 214/440 as 39.6%), and the 5-yr locoregional control rates "74.7% and 62.9% (P < .05)" are given without an arm order consistent with the failure counts. Treat the magnitude as hypothesis-generating

Adeno/adenosquamous more often IB2 (27.5% vs 20.0%), less often IIIB (21.4% vs 28.6%), more often poorly differentiated (46.2% vs 26.8%)*

notes.title: Table 2A traps
notes.md:
- Cisplatin CRT removes the RT-alone OS deficit vs SCC [4], but large series still find ADC worse with CCRT [55,56].
- No positive backbone trial prints an ADC HR; induction and cisplatin benefits are extrapolated [41,42,44,47,59].
- Tang 2012, the only ADC-only RCT, is positive but prints no HRs: hypothesis-generating [53].
- ADC responds more slowly (CR 86.5% vs 94.7%): incomplete response at 1–2 mo is not failure [54].
- Non-squamous imbalance against the worse arm in GOG-263 and TACO [28,51]; gastric-type has no CRT data [34,101].

sections.title: 3. Recurrent or metastatic disease
sections.intro: Split by line: **3A** first-line (radiosensitising cisplatin allowed), **3B** second line and beyond. The GOG non-squamous single-agent trials, the only ADC-only systemic data, sit in 3B.

notes.title: ADC relapses more often distantly after surgery [36,37], so prior-cisplatin exposure may differ from SCC-weighted trial averages; non-squamous subgroups are 90–185 patients.

SCC for comparison: OS 0.61 (0.47–0.80), PFS 0.61 (0.48–0.78) [66]. **5-year update [65]**: ITT non-squamous OS **0.75 (0.51–1.11)** (114/169) and PFS **0.64 (0.43–0.94)** (121/169); CPS ≥1 non-squamous OS 0.72 (0.46–1.12) and PFS 0.60 (0.39–0.92); ITT squamous OS 0.58 (0.46–0.73), PFS 0.58 (0.46–0.73)

cols.regimen: Cemiplimab 350 mg q3w (≤96 wk) vs investigator's-choice single-agent chemotherapy (pemetrexed, topotecan, irinotecan, gemcitabine or vinorelbine)

notes.title: Reading Table 3
notes.md:
- 3A: the non-squamous OS signal is consistent across trials, PFS is not (COMPASSION-16 PFS 0.94) [65–68].
- Backbone: keep cisplatin–paclitaxel (topotecan doublet worst in ADC, OS HR 1.58) [73]; bevacizumab's ADC benefit is uncertain (interaction P = 0.07) [71].
- 3B: cemiplimab and tisotumab vedotin OS benefits reach ADC [2,3,80]; evidence after 1L pembrolizumab is thin.
- Single agent of choice: paclitaxel (ORR 31%) [81]; PD-L1 CPS <1 is common and cemiplimab is PD-L1-unselected [16,18,80].
- HPV-independent ADC: no prospective systemic data at any line [20,87].

notes.md:

- Bevacizumab templates: GOG-240 histology interaction P = 0.07 [71]. Topotecan–cisplatin: no ADC subgroup [70,77].

cols.regimen: Induction weekly carboplatin AUC2 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² ×6 → CCRT vs CCRT
cols.pop: FIGO 2008 IB1 node-positive to IVA
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out** (stratified squamous vs non-squamous; non-squamous 89/500, 17.8%; no subgroup HR — see T2A)
cols.tox: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy before chemoradiation, not before surgery

cols.regimen: Cisplatin-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy → surgery vs CCRT
cols.pop: FIGO IB2–IIB
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: adenocarcinoma **31 (10%) vs 35 (11%)**, adenosquamous 16 (5%) vs 11 (4%) — non-squamous 93 of 626 (14.9%); randomisation stratified on cell type but no histology subgroup is reported
cols.hr: OS **0.84 (0.64–1.12)**, P = .240; PFS **0.72 (0.57–0.93)**, P = .010 — both chemoradiation vs NACT–surgery (NACT–surgery = reference)
cols.tox: Short-term grade ≥3 AE 41% vs 23%; 48% of NACT-S patients also received RT

cols.regimen: Cisplatin 50 mg/m² + vincristine 1 mg/m² D1 + bleomycin 25 mg/m² D1–3 ×3 → radical hysterectomy vs pelvic radiotherapy alone (6:4)
cols.pop: Bulky (≥4 cm) stage IB–IIA, non-small-cell carcinoma
cols.hist: **Included, not broken out**: adenocarcinoma 3 (4%) vs 4 (8%), adenosquamous 3 (4%) vs 2 (4%) — non-squamous 12 of 120 (10%); histology subgroup not reported
cols.tox: Control was RT alone

cols.regimen: Docetaxel 60 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC6 q21d ×1–3 (2 cycles in 77%) → radical hysterectomy (single arm)
cols.pop: FIGO IB2, IIA2, IIB **non-squamous** carcinoma; enrolled 2007–2010, median follow-up 1913 days
cols.n: 52 eligible (61 enrolled, 59 assessed for toxicity); 47 with central review
cols.hist: **ADC-only trial**: usual-type 20 (42.6%), **gastric-type 13 (27.7%)**, adenosquamous 12 (25.5%), small cell 1, serous 1 [101]. Response **gastric-type 46.2% vs usual-type 85.0%** (P = 0.048); microscopic downstaging of stage II: usual-type 11/16 (68.8%) vs **gastric-type 0/8** (P < 0.01); both inoperable tumours were gastric-type [101]. 50 of 52 (96%) reached radical hysterectomy
cols.dfs_pfs: 2-yr PFS **67.9%** (53.0–78.9) overall — 61.4% IB2, 71.4% IIA2, 70.0% IIB (trend P = 0.9953); by histology AC 73.1% vs adenosquamous 54.2% (P = 0.4262); pelvic nodes 47.1% vs 81.1% (P = 0.0041) and parametrial invasion 50.0% vs 77.9% (P = 0.0024). 5-yr PFS gastric-type **38.5% vs usual-type 75.0%** (P = 0.011) [101]
cols.os: 2-yr OS **85.9%** (72.7–93.0) overall — 76.9% IB2, 85.7% IIA2, 90.0% IIB in the results text (the abstract prints 81.8 / 85.7 / 92.6 for the same rates — discrepancy in the paper); 5-yr OS gastric-type **36.9% vs 90.0%** (P < 0.001) [101]
cols.tox: ORR 69% (95% CI 57–82%; 5 CR, 31 PR, 15 SD, 1 PD); grade 4 neutropenia 43/59, grade 3 11/59. The only prospective evidence that separates gastric-type from usual-type

notes.title: Reading Table 4
notes.md:
- NACT-surgery has not beaten CRT [103] and was worse for DFS in the SCC-only trial [108]; no ADC result reported.
- Gastric-type responds half as often and is never downstaged (5-yr OS 36.9% vs 90.0%): don't plan NACT-surgery [34,101].
- Induction before CRT (INTERLACE) is the one positive strategy, extrapolated to ADC [41,53]. Fertility-sparing: no RCT; ESGO excludes NHPVA [25].
